cohort: 396 primiparous adolescents (15-19 years) with singleton low-risk pregnancies, compared to 410 primiparous low-risk young adults (20-25 years)
finding: While adolescents, especially the youngest group, were less likely to have booked antenatal care and booked later in pregnancy, maternal and neonatal outcomes were comparable between adolescents and young adults.
mod_finding: Adolescents had a decreased likelihood of Caesarian section compared to young adults (20-25 years old).
